title: Universal halting is not in polynomial time
statement: For every effective machine code scheme $c$, the unary language consisting of all-one words of length $n$ such that the most-significant-first binary expansion of $n$ is $1$ followed by a string $s$ for which some advice string $\alpha$ and input $x$ satisfy $s=\langle\alpha,x\rangle$ and the machine decoded from $\alpha$ halts on $x$ with some output is not in $\mathrm{P}=\bigcup_{C\in\mathbb{N}}\mathrm{DTIME}(n\mapsto n^C+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is an effective machine code scheme
replaced:
For every effective machine representation scheme $c$, the unary language of numbers
whose binary expansions begin with $1s$, where $s$ encodes an advice string and an input
on which the machine decoded from that advice halts, is not decidable in time $n^d+1$ up
to a constant factor for any natural number $d$.
